effect_mechanism: Planted stands create habitat and attract seed dispersers: beneath framework-species plantings in northern Thailand a range of tree seedling species recruited naturally, most of them animal-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan as raising plant, habitat and animal diversity, citing snakes, lizards and turtles returning [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity].
conditionality: Agreement is split: an INRAE expert synthesis finds that plantations generally reduce biodiversity or shift composition away from native species, citing a 40% loss of local species richness relative to uncut forest, and its own small meta-analysis gives an imprecise estimate whose interval spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]; a pantropical review warns that where forests can regenerate naturally, tree planting can reduce biodiversity benefits if the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]. The negative findings come from temperate and boreal harvest-renewal settings where the comparator is natural regeneration or uncut forest rather than degraded land, while the positive side rests on compiler ratings and a case study without an unplanted control.

effect_mechanism: Assisted regeneration recovers habitat by letting canopy cover and tree density build up: WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh rate animal and habitat diversity as increased as the habitat improved, and in Niger rate plant diversity as strongly increased where assisted natural regeneration is combined with planting selected species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity]. In Brazilian restinga, artificial perches accelerated the regeneration of native animal-dispersed species, consistent with a cited study in which perches increased seed and seedling abundance and richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2].
conditionality: The low-income evidence is compiler ratings without species counts, and the measured evidence comes from a single restoration site in upper-middle-income Brazil using a specific nucleation technique, so transfer to other assisted-regeneration designs is assumed.

Soil carbon also rises: afforestation of cropland raised soil organic carbon stocks by 26% on average and tropical transitions to plantation gained 0.919% of initial soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_2], and WOCAT compilers in Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate above- or below-ground carbon as increased.
conditionality: Soil gains are conditional: on pastures (3%) and natural grasslands the change was not significant, boreal sites lost 1.5% while other zones gained 7 to 17%, low-clay soils showed no change, and heavily disturbed site preparation cut the gain to 4% against 19% with low disturbance [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_9]; that meta-analysis draws mostly on high-income temperate sites. effect_mechanism: Mangrove belts lower coastal flood impact by attenuating wind waves and, far more weakly, storm-surge water levels as water passes through the forest, with attenuation depending on inundation depth, tree species, density and creeks. A global flood model finds that losing current mangroves would increase the land, people and property flooded each year, and in Orissa, India, villages behind mangroves had fewer cyclone deaths and lower household losses; WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh and the Philippines rate flood impacts as decreased. In Bangladesh, a cited model finds 500 m mangrove afforestation patches can mitigate surge current velocities by up to 90% [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2].
conditionality: Almost all measured and modelled evidence concerns existing mangrove forests rather than restored stands, so the transfer to restoration is assumed. Measured surge reductions come from south Florida in the USA, wave reductions are upper bounds partly derived from small-wave measurements, and the Orissa household-loss comparison is a perception-based survey of a few villages. The Bangladesh study is modelled grey literature from the World Bank, and it finds mangroves have only a small effect (<4%) on design total water level because the surge dominates, so their benefit there is protection of embankments from erosion and currents rather than lower flood levels [ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_1, ev_flood_hazard_wbmang25_2].

effect_mechanism: Across restoration families the gain runs mostly through fodder and livestock: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, India, Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan rate fodder and animal production as increased, from cut-and-carry grass in enclosures, planted sand-fixing species used as forage and better grazing management. Crop gains are reported where regeneration improves soils or supplies mulch, and in Niger assisted natural regeneration in fields is reported to raise millet and sorghum output by almost 50%; in Brazil the Reflorestar payments-for-ecosystem-services programme raised agricultural value added and production value in the poorest municipalities. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and one Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged; much of the evidence is fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield. The Brazilian quasi-experimental gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state, and the source reports a heterogeneous, negative response in better-off municipalities. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].
